title: Forms and validation
summary: EditForm, input components, and data annotations.

predict.title: No validator
options: An error message *The Name field is required.* appears
Nothing happens, and no message appears
An exception, because `[Required]` needs a validator
predict.explanation: There is no **`<DataAnnotationsValidator />`**, so nobody reads the `[Required]` attribute. With no validator, every submit is valid, `OnValidSubmit` runs and the page shows **Saved**. The attributes only describe the rules; the validator component is what applies them.

predict.title: Two submit callbacks
predict.body:
```razor
<EditForm Model="model" OnSubmit="Check" OnValidSubmit="Save">
    <DataAnnotationsValidator />
    <InputText @bind-Value="model.Name" />
    <button type="submit">Save</button>
</EditForm>
```

**What happens when this component renders?**
options: `Check` runs first, then `Save` if the model is valid
An exception: `OnSubmit` can't be used together with `OnValidSubmit`
predict.explanation: `OnSubmit` means *"I'll handle validation myself"*. `OnValidSubmit` / `OnInvalidSubmit` mean *"Blazor validates for me"*. You must choose one style, so `EditForm` throws an `InvalidOperationException`. Use `OnValidSubmit` (and maybe `OnInvalidSubmit`), or only `OnSubmit` with `editContext.Validate()`.

predict.title: A static SSR form with no name
options: Nothing: a static page can't handle clicks
The POST fails with an error saying the request doesn't specify which form is being submitted
The page reloads and the email box is empty, but no error
predict.explanation: Under static SSR, submit is a real **HTTP POST** to the page. The server must know **which form** on the page was posted, and it reads that from the form name. Without **`FormName`** the server can't map the POST to a form and returns an error. Add `FormName="contact"` to the `EditForm`.

predict.title: The CSS classes
predict.explanation: When the field changes, the `EditContext` marks it **modified** and the validator checks that field. `hello` is not an email, so it is also **invalid**. The input gets `modified invalid`, which the default CSS shows with a red outline. Before you touched it, it had only `valid` (an empty value passes `[EmailAddress]`).

practice.title: Turn on validation
practice.task:
This form has a `[Required]` rule, but it saves even when the name is empty. Fix it:

1. Add the component that applies the data annotations.
2. Add a **summary** of all errors, inside the form.
3. Below the input, show the errors for **`model.Name`** only.
practice.starter:
<EditForm Model="model" OnValidSubmit="Save">

    <InputText @bind-Value="model.Name" />

    <button type="submit">Save</button>
</EditForm>

@code {
    private Person model = new();

    private void Save() { }

    public class Person
    {
        [Required] public string? Name { get; set; }
    }
}
practice.solution:
<EditForm Model="model" OnValidSubmit="Save">
    <DataAnnotationsValidator />
    <ValidationSummary />

    <InputText @bind-Value="model.Name" />
    <ValidationMessage For="() => model.Name" />

    <button type="submit">Save</button>
</EditForm>

@code {
    private Person model = new();

    private void Save() { }

    public class Person
    {
        [Required] public string? Name { get; set; }
    }
}

checks.label: Has `<DataAnnotationsValidator />`
checks.hint: Add `<DataAnnotationsValidator />` as the first thing inside the `EditForm`.

practice.title: Write the rules
practice.task:
Add data annotations to `OrderModel`:

1. **`Customer`** is required, with 2 to 50 characters.
2. **`Email`** is required and must look like an email.
3. **`Quantity`** must be between **1** and **10**.
practice.hint: `[StringLength(50, MinimumLength = 2)]`, `[EmailAddress]` and `[Range(1, 10)]`. You can stack attributes, or write `[Required, EmailAddress]`.

practice.title: Fix the broken form
practice.task:
An AI tool wrote this form. It throws when it renders, and the input doesn't bind. Fix it:

1. Keep **only** `OnValidSubmit="Save"` (remove `OnSubmit`).
2. Bind the input the way input components need.
3. Make the button submit the form.
practice.starter:
<EditForm Model="model" OnSubmit="Check" OnValidSubmit="Save">
    <DataAnnotationsValidator />
    <InputText @bind="model.Title" />
    <ValidationMessage For="() => model.Title" />
    <button type="button">Save</button>
</EditForm>
practice.hint: `OnSubmit` can't be mixed with `OnValidSubmit`. Input components use `@bind-Value`. A button submits only with `type="submit"`.

practice.title: Pick the right inputs
practice.task:
`ProfileModel` has these properties:

```csharp
public string? Bio { get; set; }          // long text
public DateOnly BirthDate { get; set; }
public bool AcceptTerms { get; set; }
public Plan Plan { get; set; }            // enum: Free, Pro
```

Inside the form, add one input component for each property, bound with `@bind-Value`:

- a multi-line text box for `Bio`
- a date box for `BirthDate`
- a checkbox for `AcceptTerms`
- a drop-down (`<select>`) for `Plan`, with an option for `Free` and one for `Pro`

checks.label: `InputSelect` bound to `model.Plan`, with `Free` and `Pro` options
checks.hint: Write `<InputSelect @bind-Value="model.Plan">` with `<option value="Free">Free</option>` and `<option value="Pro">Pro</option>` inside.

practice.title: Make it work under static SSR
practice.task:
This page has **no render mode** (static SSR). Clicking **Send** fails. Fix it:

1. Give the form the name **`contact`**.
2. Make Blazor fill **`Model`** from the posted form data.
3. Create the model in `OnInitialized` **only if it is `null`**.
4. Turn on **enhanced** form handling, so the page doesn't fully reload.
practice.hint: `FormName="contact"` and `Enhance` on the `EditForm`, `[SupplyParameterFromForm]` on the property, and `Model ??= new();`.

checks.label: `[SupplyParameterFromForm]` on the `Model` property
checks.hint: Put `[SupplyParameterFromForm]` right above `private ContactModel? Model { get; set; }`.

checks.label: `Model ??= new()`
checks.hint: Write `Model ??= new();` so the posted values are kept.

checks.label: No plain `Model = new()` that wipes the posted values

practice.title: A sign-up form, from scratch
practice.task:
Write the page **`/register`**:

- A nested class **`RegisterModel`** with:
  - **`Email`**: required, must be an email.
  - **`Password`**: required, at least 8 characters (max 100).
  - **`ConfirmPassword`**: must equal `Password`.
- A field `model` of type `RegisterModel`.
- An `EditForm` for `model` that calls **`Register`** only when the model is valid, with a validator and a summary.
- One `InputText` per property (`type="password"` for the two passwords) and a submit button.
practice.hint: Start from the theory's complete form. `[Compare(nameof(Password))]` goes on `ConfirmPassword`.

checks.label: `Email` is required and an email address
`Password` is required with a minimum length of 8

quiz.body: An `EditForm` sets both `Model="model"` and `EditContext="editContext"`. What happens?
options: Both work, and the form validates twice
quiz.explanation: `EditForm` needs exactly one of them. With `Model`, it creates the `EditContext` for you. With `EditContext`, you created it yourself. Both at once throws an `InvalidOperationException`.

quiz.body: Which line shows the validation errors for `model.Email` only?
quiz.explanation: `For` takes a **lambda expression** that points to the property. Blazor reads the expression to find the field (the model object and the property name). A plain value or a string can't tell it which field you mean.

quiz.body: `[Required] public int Quantity { get; set; }`. The user leaves the number box empty and submits. Why does validation pass?
options: An `int` always has a value (`0`), so `[Required]` never fails. Use `int?`
It doesn't pass: the message *The Quantity field is required.* appears
quiz.explanation: `[Required]` fails only for `null` (or an empty string). An `int` is never `null`, so the rule can't fail. Make the property `int?` to know if the user filled it, or use `[Range(1, ...)]` to reject `0`.

quiz.body: Which input component do you use for a `bool` property like `AcceptTerms`?
quiz.explanation: `InputCheckbox` renders `<input type="checkbox">` and binds to a `bool` with `@bind-Value`.

quiz.body: Why does an `EditForm` in a **static SSR** page need `FormName`?
options: To set the `name` attribute used by CSS
So the antiforgery token can be generated
Because submit is a real POST, and the server must know **which form** on the page was posted
quiz.explanation: Under static SSR, there is no live connection. The browser POSTs the form to the page, and the server renders the page again. The form name in the POST tells it which form (and which handler) to use. It must be unique on the page.

quiz.body: What does `[SupplyParameterFromForm]` on a property do?
options: Makes the property a parameter the parent must set
On a form POST, fills the property from the posted form data
Saves the property in the browser between visits
Validates the property with data annotations
quiz.explanation: On a POST, Blazor binds the form fields to this property (`Model.Email` from the field named `Model.Email`, and so on). On a GET it stays `null`, which is why you write `Model ??= new()` in `OnInitialized`.

quiz.body: What does the `Enhance` parameter on an `EditForm` do?
options: Sends the POST with `fetch` and patches the new HTML into the page, with no full reload
Validates each field while the user types
quiz.explanation: `Enhance` turns on **enhanced form handling**. It is still a POST and the page is still static SSR, but Blazor sends it in the background and updates the DOM, so the scroll position and page state are kept. On a plain `<form>`, use `data-enhance`.

quiz.body: A static SSR page uses a plain HTML `<form method="post" @formname="search">` instead of `EditForm`. The POST is rejected. What is missing?
quiz.explanation: `app.UseAntiforgery()` rejects POSTs without a valid token. `EditForm` adds the token for you, but a plain `<form>` doesn't, so add `<AntiforgeryToken />` inside it.

options: When an input loses focus with a bad value
When the form is submitted and validation **fails**
When the server returns an error
quiz.explanation: `OnInvalidSubmit` runs on submit when the `EditContext` has errors, `OnValidSubmit` when it has none. You can use both on the same form, for example to show a toast when the form is invalid.

quiz.body: Where does `[Compare]` go to check that the two passwords match?
options: On both properties, each pointing to the other
quiz.explanation: `[Compare]` goes on the property being checked, and names the **other** property it must equal. Put it on `ConfirmPassword`, so the error shows next to the confirm field.

interview.question: What is `EditForm`, and what does it do?
interview.modelAnswer: A component that renders a `<form>` for a model. It creates an `EditContext` that tracks which fields changed and which have errors, shares it with the inputs and validators inside, and calls `OnValidSubmit` or `OnInvalidSubmit` when the form is submitted.

interview.question: What is the difference between `OnSubmit`, `OnValidSubmit` and `OnInvalidSubmit`?
interview.modelAnswer: `OnValidSubmit` runs only when validation passes, `OnInvalidSubmit` only when it fails, and you can use both together. `OnSubmit` runs on every submit and leaves validation to you (`editContext.Validate()`). `OnSubmit` can't be combined with the other two.

interview.question: How do data annotations become validation in a Blazor form?
interview.modelAnswer: You put attributes like `[Required]`, `[StringLength]`, `[Range]`, `[EmailAddress]` and `[Compare]` on the model's properties. Then `<DataAnnotationsValidator />` inside the `EditForm` reads them and adds errors to the `EditContext`. Without that component, the attributes do nothing.

interview.question: How do you show validation errors to the user?
interview.modelAnswer: `<ValidationSummary />` shows all errors in a list. `<ValidationMessage For="() => model.Name" />` shows the errors for one field. The inputs also get the `valid`, `invalid` and `modified` CSS classes, so the field can be styled.

interview.question: Why do input components use `@bind-Value` and not `@bind`?
interview.modelAnswer: They are components with a `Value` parameter, so you bind to that parameter with `@bind-Value`. It also passes `ValueChanged` and a `ValueExpression`, and the expression tells the input which model field it edits, so validation can mark that field. `@bind` is for plain HTML elements.

interview.question: When would you pass an `EditContext` instead of a `Model`?
interview.modelAnswer: When I need the `EditContext` in code: to call `Validate()` myself, check `IsModified()`, listen to `OnFieldChanged`, or add custom validation messages. Otherwise `Model` is simpler. You must set one or the other, never both.

interview.question: How does a form work in a static SSR page?
interview.modelAnswer: Submit is a real HTTP POST to the page. The `EditForm` needs a unique `FormName` so the server knows which form was posted, and the model property needs `[SupplyParameterFromForm]` so Blazor fills it from the form data. You create the model with `Model ??= new()`. `Enhance` avoids a full page reload.

interview.question: What is the antiforgery token, and how does Blazor use it?
interview.modelAnswer: A hidden token that proves the POST came from your own page, which protects against cross-site request forgery. `app.UseAntiforgery()` checks it on POST requests. `EditForm` adds the token automatically; a plain `<form>` needs `<AntiforgeryToken />`.
